trust_decision.summary: SigV4 verification decides whether the request's x-amz-* headers (which select and parameterise the S3 operation, e.g. x-amz-copy-source) are covered by the signature; at the pinned commit only x-amz-meta-* is compared (presigned only) and the Authorization-header path checks nothing, so an unsigned x-amz-copy-source turns a signed/presigned PUT into a server-side copy.

landing_point.why: Advisory summary names extractSignedHeaders() in cmd/signature-v4-utils.go; checkMetaHeaders sits right below at cmd/signature-v4-utils.go:268.

fix_sites.entry_point: every SigV4-authenticated S3/STS/admin request via reqSignatureV4Verify (cmd/auth-handler.go:612-621); exploited via PUT /{bucket}/{object} with x-amz-copy-source (CopyObject, CopyObjectPart)
fix_sites.module_kind: auth verifier helper (checkMetaHeaders -> checkUnsignedHeaders: all x-amz-*, membership test, two exemptions)

fix_sites.entry_point: presigned SigV4 URL on any S3 route (doesPresignedSignatureMatch, cmd/auth-handler.go:617-618)
Authorization-header SigV4 on any S3 route, plus admin (cmd/auth-handler.go:172) and STS (cmd/sts-handlers.go:221) via isReqAuthenticated
fix_sites.module_kind: auth verifier, header implementation (check newly added; never existed here)

fix_sites.entry_point: presigned SigV4 (writes x-amz-signature-age scratch header after verification)
fix_sites.module_kind: auth verifier side effect consumed by policy conditions
handler that synthesises x-amz-tagging from the body; moved after authenticateRequest so the new check does not reject it

fix_sites.entry_point: policy condition evaluation (s3:signatureAge) for all authorised requests

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: cmd/streaming-signature-v4.go:126-131 (calculateSeedSignature: separate SigV4 seed verifier for STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-PAYLOAD; NOT touched by the published fix, recorded also as O8)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory's exploit is x-amz-copy-source, and CopyObject/CopyObjectPart reject streaming auth outright (cmd/auth-handler.go:375-376), so the chunked-upload seed verifier looks like a payload-only path that cannot be confused into a copy.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate x-amz-* headers the server or clients send unsigned must keep working: PutObjectTagging synthesises x-amz-tagging before auth (must move after auth), the presigned verifier writes x-amz-signature-age into r.Header and re-verification must still pass, and clients send x-amz-content-sha256 unsigned. A blanket 'all x-amz-* must be signed' breaks tagging, s3:signatureAge policies and idempotent re-verify.

O6_input_shapes: any x-amz-* header name, not only x-amz-meta-* (case-insensitive prefix)
multi-value header whose first value is empty (membership test instead of value equality; old code compared val[0] at cmd/signature-v4-utils.go:272)
exempt shapes: x-amz-content-sha256 unsigned, x-amz-signature-age scratch header

O7_producer.where: cmd/object-handlers.go:3662 (x-amz-tagging synthesised from XML body before authenticateRequest at cmd/object-handlers.go:3666); cmd/signature-v4.go:338 (x-amz-signature-age written by verifier, read at cmd/bucket-policy.go:258)

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Copy-source confused deputy is unreachable with streaming auth (cmd/auth-handler.go:375-376); looks like a body-chunk signature path, separate file from the advisory's landing point
